prompt: Implement unify_types(equations), a deterministic finite first-order type-equation solver. This is a declared algebraic subset, not a source-language parser, full Hindley–Milner inference engine or compiler. Types have exactly one of these native representations: the string 'Bool' or 'Nat'; {var:NAME}; or {arrow:[TYPE,TYPE]}. NAME is one lowercase ASCII letter a through h. Every type is a finite tree with input depth at most 4 (leaves have depth 0). equations is a native list of at most 16 two-element lists [left_type,right_type], with at most 100 type nodes total across the input. Process equations in list order. For each equation, first recursively apply the current substitution to BOTH sides. Identical resolved types succeed without a new binding, including a variable equated with itself. If two distinct variables remain, bind the lexically larger name to the smaller. If exactly one side is a variable, bind it to the other resolved type only when that type does not contain the variable anywhere; a proper occurrence fails the whole system. If both sides are arrows, recursively unify their domain children first, then their result children under the updated substitution. Unequal constants, or a constant versus an arrow, fail. On failure return exactly {ok:False,substitution:{}}; expose no partial bindings. On success return exactly {ok:True,substitution:{NAME:TYPE,...}}, including EVERY variable appearing anywhere in the original input, even when its final value is the unchanged {var:NAME}. Fully resolve all substitution chains and constructor children. Dictionary ordering is irrelevant; the lexical variable-binding rule fixes otherwise equivalent representative choices. For this bounded domain, every finite resolved tree produced while following this procedure has at most 2048 nodes; cyclic input trees and outside-domain validation are excluded. Empty input is valid and succeeds with an empty substitution. Containers and scalars must be exact native dict/list/str/bool values as specified. Never mutate inputs, including during later calls. Every output mutable container must be fresh, independent of all other output containers, earlier calls and inputs, including repeated equal type subtrees. Use only the standard library, with no compiler invocation, external solver, raw memory, threads or network. Earlier returned values and their native types must remain unchanged during later calls.

Implement generalize_instantiate(inferred, environment, substitution, count=2), a finite scheme-normalization/generalization model, not full program inference or compilation. Type is exactly native string 'Bool' or 'Nat', {var:ID}, or {from:Type,to:Type}. Scheme is exactly {bound:[distinct_type_variable_IDs],body:Type}; forall occurs only at this outer wrapper. IDs match case-sensitive ASCII [a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,11}; term-binding and type-variable namespaces are separate. environment is a native dict of 0–6 term bindings to schemes, each with at most 4 bound variables. substitution is a native dict of 0–8 type-variable IDs to Types. Every input Type has at most 31 type nodes and depth at most 6 (leaves have depth 0). count is a native int 0–4 excluding bool, default 2. The substitution key-dependency graph is acyclic, including no self-edge. All transitively expanded ranges/types in the stated algorithm have at most 127 nodes and depth at most 12. Inputs satisfy these bounds; no outside-domain validation is required. Treat substitution as an acyclic variable-binding store: recursively resolve its replacement variables to completion, not just one simultaneous substitution pass. Normalize inferred with that store. For each environment scheme, substitute only free variables and avoid capture with this exact deterministic policy. First compute R, the union of free variables in all fully normalized substitution ranges. In lexically sorted environment-binding order, visit each scheme's bound list in its supplied order; rename exactly those binders whose names lie in R, including unused binders. Rename their bound occurrences consistently before substituting free variables with normalized ranges; shield all resulting binders. A bound name that is also a substitution key is not itself replaced. This deliberately conservative alpha-renaming policy fixes the output even when a colliding range is unused by that scheme. One per-call fresh supply emits t0,t1,..., skipping every type-variable name anywhere in inferred, environment bound lists/bodies, substitution keys/ranges and every name already generated. Term-binding names do not reserve type-variable names. This supply first serves environment alpha-renaming, then instance generation. Preserve each environment bound list's order after renaming. Let GammaPrime be the normalized environment; scheme free variables exclude its bound list. Generalize exactly the lexically sorted set FV(normalized_type)-FV(GammaPrime). The new scheme uses that bound list and the normalized type as its body. For each of count instances, replace each newly generalized variable in sorted bound order with one fresh name from the same supply, consistently throughout that instance, preserving free variables. Empty generalization still produces count independent bodies with empty renaming maps. Return exactly {normalized_type:Type,environment:{term:Scheme},scheme:Scheme,instances:[{renaming:{bound_variable:fresh_variable},body:Type}]}. Dictionary ordering is irrelevant; instance order and all stated lists are significant. All containers/scalars are the exact native dict/list/str/int forms stated, and every mutable output container is fresh and independent of inputs, all other output containers and earlier call results, including repeated equal subtrees. Never mutate inputs, including during later calls. Earlier returned values and their native types must remain unchanged during later calls. No unification, recursive types, mutable effects or arbitrary Hindley–Milner program evaluation is performed. Use only the standard library with no external solver/compiler, raw memory, threads or network.

Implement assignability_matrix(parents, sources, targets, strict_function_types=True). This is a declared finite constructor/type algebra using scoped variance policies, not a full TypeScript/Java compiler or structural-member inference engine. parents is a native dict with 0–8 opaque case-sensitive ASCII type IDs matching [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,15}. Each value is a native list of distinct direct supertype IDs present as keys. There are no self edges or cycles; multiple inheritance and unrelated roots are allowed. Base S<:T means S==T or a path from S through parents reaches T. There is no implicit universal top, bottom, any, union, coercion or special void-return rule; IDs have only their declared graph meaning. sources and targets are native lists of 0–12 descriptors. A descriptor is exactly {kind,type} for kind in 'value','producer','consumer','cell', or {kind,arg,result} for kind in 'property','method'; every referenced type ID exists. The constructor kinds are disjoint in THIS algebra, so different kinds are not assignable; this is not a claim about real TypeScript cross-syntax conversions. For equal kinds, source is assignable to target under these rules: value/producer requires source.type<:target.type; consumer requires target.type<:source.type; cell requires identical type IDs; property requires source.result<:target.result and, when strict_function_types=True, target.arg<:source.arg, otherwise either parameter subtype direction; method requires source.result<:target.result and either parameter subtype direction regardless of the strict flag. strict_function_types is a native bool, default True. Every function descriptor has one required argument and the stated ordinary result; no overloads, optional/rest parameters or generic call signatures are modeled. Return a native list of rows in source order, each containing one exact native bool per target in target order. Empty sources returns []; empty targets gives a distinct fresh empty row per source. Inputs satisfy all domain constraints; no outside-domain validation is required. All containers/scalars have the stated exact built-in dict/list/str/bool types. Inputs remain unchanged during this and later calls. Every returned mutable container must be distinct from inputs, other returned containers and earlier call results. Use only the standard library and ordinary Python computation/allocation; no real compiler/runtime invocation, raw memory, threads or network. Earlier returned values and their native types must remain unchanged during later calls.

Implement enum_match_analysis(variants, arms, values, non_exhaustive=False, outside_crate=False), a finite Rust1.90-inspired coverage/selection model, not compiler execution. variants is an ordered native list of 0–8 distinct case-sensitive ASCII IDs matching [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,15}. Every listed variant is inhabited and has no modeled payload. arms is an ordered native list of 0–16 exact {pattern,guard} dicts. pattern is a declared variant ID or '*' wildcard; guard is None for UNGUARDED or a guard ID using the same ASCII grammar. Guard IDs may repeat; guard and variant namespaces are separate, and '*' cannot be a variant ID. values is a native list of 0–12 exact {tag,guards} dicts. tag is a declared variant ID, or None for a symbolic future variant ONLY when non_exhaustive AND outside_crate are True. Each guards dict contains exactly all distinct guard IDs mentioned in arms, mapped to native bool outcomes; the modeled predicates are pure and stable within that value's evaluation. Both flags are native bool, default False. Static coverage counts ONLY unguarded patterns, even if a guard is true for every supplied sample. An unguarded named arm covers its known variant; an unguarded '*' covers all known variants and the possible future alternative. Future coverage is required exactly when both flags are True. For each runtime value independently, scan arms in order. A named pattern matches only an equal known tag; '*' matches known and future tags. Nonmatching patterns do not test their guards. A matching guarded arm tests its supplied Boolean and is selected only if true; a matching unguarded arm selects immediately. Stop at the first selected arm. Return exactly {missing,future_missing,exhaustive,decisions}. missing lists known uncovered variants in original variants order. future_missing is a native bool. exhaustive is true exactly when missing is empty and future_missing is false. decisions contains one exact {selected,tested_guards} record per value in value order: selected is the zero-based native int arm index or None; tested_guards lists the native int indices of matching guarded arms actually tested in order, including a selected guarded arm. The diagnostic model still calculates selections for statically incomplete arm sets; it does not claim Rust executes rejected source or permits fabricating future variants in safe current Rust. Unreachable later arms are allowed as analyzer inputs; redundancy diagnostics are not modeled. Empty lists are allowed subject to tag validity: an empty closed domain is exhaustively covered without arms, while an external non_exhaustive empty known domain still requires future coverage. Inputs meet all schemas/preconditions, so no outside-domain validation is required. All containers/scalars use the stated exact built-in dict/list/str/int/bool/None types; output index ints exclude bool. Inputs and earlier results must remain unchanged during this and later calls. Every returned mutable container must be distinct from every input, other returned container and earlier call result. Use only the standard library and ordinary Python computation/allocation; no real compiler/runtime invocation, raw memory, threads or network.

Implement validate_record(value), an explicit bounded runtime shape gate over tagged values, not TypeScript/JavaScript interpretation or implicit annotation enforcement. A Primitive is exactly {tag:'undefined'}, {tag:'null'}, {tag:'boolean',value:bool}, {tag:'number',value:int}, or {tag:'string',value:str}. Numeric payloads are native non-bool integers in [-1000,1000], an exactly representable subset of JavaScript Number; strings have 0–32 printable ASCII characters (U+0020 through U+007E). An Object is exactly {tag:'object',own:{key:Primitive},inherited:{key:Primitive}}. Each map has 0–8 case-sensitive keys matching ASCII [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,15}; own and inherited may contain the same key. Fields are primitive only: no nested objects, accessors or proxies. inherited explicitly summarizes prototype-visible data fields; no actual JavaScript object/prototype lookup occurs. Top-level value is one Primitive or one Object. Every input encoding is well formed; invalid schemas are outside the domain. Apply this fixed application policy: require an Object with an OWN name whose tag is string; the empty string is valid. Optional age depends on OWN presence. Absent own age is allowed regardless of inherited age. Present own age must have number tag; present undefined is rejected, not treated as absent. All modeled numeric payloads, including negative ages, are accepted: this is a type/shape gate, not an age-plausibility rule. Other own/inherited fields are ignored. Inherited name never satisfies the own-name requirement or repairs a mistyped own name. Return exactly {ok:bool,errors:[error_codes],data:None_or_dict}. For a non-object, return ok=False, errors=['object-required'], data=None without checking fields. For an object, first report 'name-missing' if own lacks name, otherwise 'name-type' if its tag is not string; then append 'age-type' if own age exists with a non-number tag. Collect both errors when applicable and preserve this exact order; no other errors are returned. Any error means data=None. Otherwise return ok=True, errors=[], data={name:unchanged_string_payload}, adding age:unchanged_integer_payload only for a valid OWN age. Project only these validated fields, without inherited or extra properties. None is an output failure marker; undefined and null inputs remain distinct tagged records. All containers/scalars use the exact native dict/list/str/int/bool/None types specified. No coercion or outside-domain validation is required. Every returned mutable container must be fresh, pairwise independent and unaliased to any input or earlier call result. Never mutate inputs, including during later calls. Earlier returned values and their native types must remain unchanged during later calls. The optional-field rule is an explicitly implemented runtime analogue of the stated presence distinction, not a claim that TypeScript inserts a validator. Use only the standard library and ordinary computation/allocation, with no actual compiler/runtime invocation, raw memory, threads or network.
